description: Formalizing artisanal cobalt mining: EGC finally gets moving in 2025-2026
verification_status: confirmed by multiple sources; final 2026 figures come from trade media (trendsnafrica.com), sourced to EGC's CEO speaking at the MOTA conference

background.creation: Entreprise Generale du Cobalt (EGC) - a state monopoly on buying artisanal cobalt, created by decree in November 2019, announced in March 2021
background.goal: formalize 40 artisanal mining zones (ZEAs), improve safety, eliminate child labor
background.2019_2024_problem: the company was effectively dormant for nearly five years due to internal conflicts; a pilot at Mutoshi (with Trafigura and Chemaf) was suspended for COVID in 2020 and never resumed
background.artisanal_share: 10-30% of DRC cobalt (estimates vary); per Pact, 10-12% of world cobalt output comes from DRC's artisanal sector

2025_2026_breakthrough.first_batch: 1,000 t of fully traceable artisanal cobalt - November 2025
2025_2026_breakthrough.export_via_lobito: EGC became the first Congolese company to export cobalt via the Lobito corridor - about 3,000 t in H1 2026
2025_2026_breakthrough.quota_utilization: used '100% of its quota' allocated by ARECOMS, versus a national average of about 60%

partnerships.content: MoU at Mining Indaba: ERG transfers a Lualaba site to EGC for an artisanal zone
allocation of sites to set up ZEAs

2025_2026_breakthrough.technical_support: GIZ (Cobalt for Development Programme), coordination with ARECOMS, SEAMAPE, and CEEC
2025_2026_breakthrough.outlook: EGC states a goal of developing its own refining and battery manufacturing domestically

remaining_problems.afrewatch_2023: the allocated artisanal zone was deemed insufficient; large companies are reluctant to give up parts of their concessions, citing security risks and the fact they already pay for the land
remaining_problems.informal_sector_persists: per Mongabay (Oct 2024), at the Mutoshi pilot site, after formalization collapsed in 2021, the number of artisanal miners grew almost fivefold (to ~15,000) as fencing and the ID system were dismantled
remaining_problems.accidents: AFREWATCH regularly documents collapses at artisanal sites (e.g., two collapses in May 2025 at the COMIDE/ERG license near Kisankala, with casualties whose numbers authorities have not disclosed)
remaining_problems.2026_fatal_incident: a mine collapse in Goma, February 2026 - over 300 dead, more than 100 missing (per Prospect-intel; relates to artisanal mining broadly, not necessarily cobalt specifically)

child_labor_estimates.ilo_cotecco_project: funded by the US Department of Labor ($5.5m), implemented by the ILO - monitors and works to eliminate child labor in the cobalt supply chain
child_labor_estimates.estimated_number_of_children: roughly 25,000-40,000 children at artisanal cobalt mines across sources (African Elements/The Conversation - 40,000; other sources - at least 25,000)
child_labor_estimates.2024_us_dol_estimate: per the user's original document (not independently re-verified this round) - over three-quarters of artisanal miners may work under conditions bearing indicators of forced labor
